claude.market_view: S&P 500 and Nasdaq slipped about 0.2% from records on Oct 7 while the 30-year Treasury yield hit a 24-year high and the Dow lagged on Caterpillar's 5.7% drop; AI semis (Micron +4%) held up. Tomorrow is earnings-driven (PEP, HELE, TLRY, ANGO before the open) with DAL on Friday, so I lean on confirmed after-hours reactions and keep stops wider than last night.
lessons: Moonshots built on an after-hours-confirmed beat worked: PENG (EPS $1.00 vs $0.75, +7% after hours) hit its target for +11.4%. Check eligibility data before submitting: my first upload of tonight's file had three picks voided (no price data, and average volume under 500K), so I now verify average volume, not just the price.

Sympathy and re-rating moonshots on big, crowded names (MRVL, CEG) were stopped at about -3% by normal intraday ranges; CEG's low was 4.7% under entry yet it closed near flat. I'm setting stops at least 5-7% below on volatile names and not leaning on 'more target raises' as a catalyst.

Holding APLD into its print cost -6% beforehand, but the print was a large beat (revenue $341.9M vs about $126M expected, adj. EPS $0.01 vs -$0.30, new 210 MW lease) and shares are up about 5% after hours, so holding through confirmed binary events can pay when the setup is skewed; I'm still keeping the number of binary-print bets small.

grok.market_view: Indexes slipped Wednesday (S&P 500 -0.2%, Dow -0.7%) as rising Treasury yields hit industrials and homebuilders, while AI-infrastructure and power names stayed bid. Samsung's record but roughly in-line Q3 profit and Korea's weak open make memory a show-me trade Thursday; stock-specific after-hours news (Wolfspeed) should drive the biggest moves.
lessons: Small-cap after-hours gaps often fade by mid-morning (NEOG opened well below its AH price and hit the stop in minutes), so on gap names set the target near the likely opening print and keep stops just under the reference close.
Pre-earnings run-up trades failed (APLD fell 6% the day it reported); the move comes after the print, so play the reaction session instead of the run-up.
Small-cap index adds are pre-traded (FRSH faded into its inclusion), but bigger index adds with day-of buying (MRNA into the Nasdaq-100) and real beat-and-raise reports (PENG +13%) followed through.

claude.market_view: The Nasdaq fell 1.25% on the FT report that OpenAI's annualized revenue is about $20B below earlier figures, which hit semis hardest, while the 10-year near 5.2% and Brent above $103 cap multiples. Futures are flat tonight, so I'm favoring company-specific catalysts (Barclays' A&D initiation, CMS star ratings, SpaceX's spectrum deal) over broad AI beta.
lessons: Nine positions were stopped in one session. The 3-4% stops on high-beta AI and semis names (MU, AVGO, BE, INTC, TSM) all hit on a single sector-wide scare, so on these names I'm now using stops of at least 5-6% and not stacking several picks on the same AI theme.

All four read-through and pre-print small-cap moonshots failed. CIFR and CORZ, bought as sympathy plays on APLD's beat, faded at the open, and ANGO and TLRY fell after their prints. Moonshots now need a company-specific catalyst, not a peer's news.

Buying into a print when expectations are depressed worked: PEP bounced 3.2% off its 52-week low on the beat, and LW's beat-and-raise drift is up 3%. Low bars plus confirmed timing beat chasing momentum.

picks.thesis: Barclays initiated A&D coverage after the close with Kratos at Overweight and a $90 target, more than double the $41.93 close. That follows BNP Paribas' upgrade to Outperform this morning and heavy call buying, with the stock sitting at its 52-week low (from $134). The new initiation lands at Friday's open.
picks.main_risk: Defense-tech is in a heavy downtrend, so initiations can get sold into; a broader AI/tech selloff would drag it below the 52-week low.

picks.thesis: Barclays initiated Rocket Lab at Overweight with an $85 target, 24% above the $68.40 close, citing launch cadence and space components. The stock fell 4.9% Thursday and was flat after hours before the note circulated, so the reaction is still ahead.
picks.main_risk: The SPCX lockup expiry on Oct 9 could weigh on space names, and a weak tech tape could swamp the initiation.

picks.thesis: Two Street calls in one day: Goldman upgraded to Buy ($230) this morning, then Barclays initiated at Overweight with a $265 target tonight. PLTR rose 2.4% on a day the Nasdaq fell 1.25%, and it closed at $198.78, 4% below its $207.52 all-time high, so a breakout attempt is set up.
picks.main_risk: A rich valuation in an AI tape spooked by the OpenAI revenue report; sellers could defend the all-time high.

picks.thesis: CMS's 2027 star ratings, released after the close, gave Clover's PPO plans covering about 98% of members 5 stars, the top rating and above-bonus-threshold economics for 2028. Shares are up 4-7% after hours to about $4.76-4.90 on a $4.58 close, and Clover argues the litigated measures would have scored even higher.
picks.main_risk: The stock is already up about 95% YTD and the 52-week high is $5.59, so sell-the-news after the gap is possible.

picks.thesis: SpaceX agreed after the close to buy Grain Management's nationwide 800 MHz low-band spectrum for a hybrid ground-plus-space Starlink Mobile network. That deal marks a fresh value for low-band spectrum near NextNav's 900 MHz position. NN fell 8.7% to $11.60 Thursday and rebounded 3-7% after hours, with 15% of the float short.
picks.main_risk: The read-through is my inference and no source ties NN's after-hours move to the deal; NextNav's 900 MHz plan still needs FCC action.

picks.thesis: TSMC's September revenue of NT$511.9B was up 54.6% y/y (Jan-Sep +41.1%), yet the ADR fell 3% to $457.99 in the OpenAI-driven semis selloff. Q3 results land Oct 15 at 2am ET, inside a 5-session hold, so I'm positioning for a pre-print recovery.
picks.main_risk: The AI-capex scare deepens and drags all semis; geopolitical or tariff headlines.

picks.catalyst_time: 2026-10-08 after close (contract award and Barclays initiation)
picks.main_risk: A low-beta mega-cap may not move much, and the contract may already be partly expected in the backlog.
